patient_information: A 23-year-old HIV-positive Zambian woman, unmarried with three children, works in a hospital cafeteria, diagnosed with HIV 1 month prior, not on ART, taking co-trimoxazole prophylaxis for 7 days, successfully treated for pulmonary tuberculosis 4 years ago, does not drink alcohol or use recreational drugs.
history_of_present_illness: The seizure occurred out of sleep, characterized by unresponsiveness and generalized shaking of all four limbs for 5 to 10 minutes, observed by her son.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Patient is a 23-year-old HIV-positive Zambian woman.
physical_exam: Patient looks well, GCS 15/15, no meningism, clear chest, and unremarkable neurological examination.
labs_and_diagnostics: Malaria rapid diagnostic test negative, blood results showed hemoglobin 11.0 g/dL (ref 12-14), CD4 count 153 cells/µL (ref 500-1200), other values normal. Lumbar puncture revealed normal opening pressure, clear CSF, CSF protein 0.78 g/L (ref 0.25-0.55), CSF glucose 2.9 mmol/L (ref 2.25-2.97*), and negative Cryptococcal antigen, India Ink, Gram, and Ziehl-Neelsen stains. EEG showed focal slowing in the right hemisphere. CT scan of the brain revealed frontal and parietal hypodense lesions in the white matter of the right hemisphere without contrast enhancement.
differential_diagnosis: Tuberculoma, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), cerebral toxoplasmosis, cryptococcoma, brain abscess, primary CNS lymphoma, and neurocysticercosis.
management_and_clinical_course: Patient was started on carbamazepine 200 mg bid, could not afford valproic acid. JC-virus DNA detected in CSF. She was commenced on ART and remained on carbamazepine, remaining seizure-free. Carbamazepine was stopped after 6 months. After 1 year of ART, CD4 count reached 535 cells/µL and she returned to work.
